subject: Follow-up: Atlantech discovery — p95 targets, streaming UX & concurrency
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Chen <sophie@atlantech.com>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@atlantech.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-28T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Follow-up: Atlantech discovery — p95 targets, streaming UX & concurrency

Thanks Sophie and Alex — good conversation earlier. Quick recap from our side plus proposed next steps so we have alignment before the SE/technical session. I captured what you emphasized on latency/throughput and streaming UX.

High-level pain points (what you told us)
- Intermittent spikes in tail latency: p95 for generation endpoints commonly 800–1,200ms for 512-token responses; this causes UI freezing and dropped streaming sessions.
- Streaming UX: partial token latency and first-byte delay leads to timeouts in your mobile client; users expect immediate token flow for short replies.
- Concurrency & burst: typical background traffic is ~200 qps peak for short sync calls; streaming concurrent connections can hit 120–150 during onboarding flows.
- Cost + ops: tight unit-cost budget; prefer optimizations that avoid a 2–3x increase in infra spend.

Current stack notes (as discussed)
- On-prem Kubernetes + Triton gRPC endpoints; model hosted in-house with a load balancer in front.
- Model: mix of open LLMs for assistant and a custom fine-tuned variant.
- Client: mobile web + native with aggressive connection timeouts (3–5s default).

Success criteria you asked for
- Short responses (<=128 tokens): p95 < 250ms.
- Mid responses (<=512 tokens): p95 < 400ms.
- Streaming responsiveness: first-byte < 200ms and sustained token latency under 50ms median once stream established.
- Scalability: sustain 250 concurrent streaming sessions with <5% tail error rate.

Proposed next steps (action items)
1) I will share a short performance matrix and a draft MOP (attached) that maps configuration options (batching, warmup, quantization) to expected p95 improvements.
2) Schedule an SE deep-dive (60–90m) focused on Triton tuning, warmup strategies, and streaming keepalive/buffering parameters — propose Dec 1 or Dec 2.
3) If agreeable, start a 2-week dedicated-capacity trial (we can scope model variant and quantization) week of Dec 6.
4) You to share sample request shape (typical token distributions) and a short extract of production logs (trace of 10 suspect requests).

Attachments: redwood-performance-matrix.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); mop-draft.xlsx (Excel, 24KB)

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll book the SE slot and send calendar invites.

Best,
Marcus Lin

marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0198

Subject: SE follow-up: preliminary config & trial plan (Atlantech)

Hi Sophie / Alex — thanks for confirming Dec 1 at 10am PT. A few technical notes ahead of the SE call and assumed answers — feel free to push back.

Preliminary recommendations (what we’ll walk through in the SE session)
- Model variant: run the custom model on a mixed-precision path; for latency-sensitive short responses test FP16 with per-channel quantization for larger layers. If a >2x speed-up is required, we’ll trial INT8 quantization in a staging pass (we’ll validate regen quality with your eval prompts).
- Batching: for short requests prioritize low-batch (<8) continuous batching with adaptive windows (2–5ms target batching window) to avoid adding 50–100ms of queuing. For mid/long responses consider dynamic batching thresholds by request size.
- Warmup: recommend a small warm pool per replica (5–10 prewarmed contexts) and keepalive TTL ~60s for active app servers; avoid very short client-side timeouts that can cause half-open streams.
- Streaming: set initial chunk size to 1–2 tokens and enable small-server-side flush (20–30ms) to give smooth token flow for mobile clients; tune socket keepalives to avoid mid-stream disconnects.
- KV/prefix caching: for assistant seed prompts, cache the KV for the first 8 tokens of the context to reduce repeated recomputation for prompt-heavy flows.

Expected improvements (estimates)
- Short responses (<=128): expect p95 drop toward ~220–300ms on dedicated capacity + FP16 + batching windows tuned.
- Medium (<=512): expect p95 ~350–450ms depending on token distribution and batch mix.
- Streaming first-byte: with small chunk + flush we generally hit <150–200ms first-byte in our trials.

Proposed trial scope & dates
- SE deep-dive: Dec 1, 10am PT (60–90m) — agenda: warmup, batching, quantization plan, monitoring hooks.
- Dedicated trial: target week of Dec 6 — 2 weeks, we’ll provision a dedicated pool, run a small load test, and measure p95 at the client-side with sample prompts you provide.
- Deliverables: config MOP (attached), runbook for warmup and streaming tuning, and a performance report at end of trial.

Attachments: mop-draft.xlsx, redwood-performance-matrix.pdf

Next asks from Atlantech
- Send model name(s) and representative token distribution (CSV or sample requests).
- Confirm team members for the SE session and one technical contact who can provide logs / access.

I’ll attach a draft runbook section in the drive after the call for you to comment on.

Thanks — looking forward to the session.

Regards,
Priyom Das
